findings.title: ValidationError used but import not shown in diff
findings.evidence: The new branch raises a ValidationError symbol that never appears elsewhere in the visible diff; the only guard is the module-level ALLOWED_TAGS set.
findings.recommendation: Confirm app/forms.py actually imports ValidationError (e.g. 'from django.core.exceptions import ValidationError' or a project-local equivalent). If it is not imported, every rejected tag raises NameError and surfaces as a 500 instead of a validation error; add the import in this same change.

findings.title: clean_tag changed from normalising to rejecting; callers may not handle the new exception
findings.evidence: Previously clean_tag returned a normalised string for any input; it now raises for anything outside ALLOWED_TAGS, so any caller that only strips/lowercases (or reads a persisted legacy tag not in the set) will now throw instead of returning a value.
findings.evidence_quote: if len(tag) > 40 or tag not in ALLOWED_TAGS:
findings.recommendation: Audit all call sites of clean_tag in this change: any path that feeds user input or stored rows must catch ValidationError and convert it into a form error, and existing rows with tags outside ALLOWED_TAGS need a migration/backfill plan before the guard goes live.

findings.title: Non-string input raises AttributeError instead of ValidationError
findings.evidence: The function calls .strip()/.lower() on raw before any type check, so a missing/None field value bypasses the intended validation path with an AttributeError rather than a clean validation failure.
findings.recommendation: Guard the type first, e.g. 'if not isinstance(raw, str): raise ValidationError("unknown tag")' (or let the form layer coerce), so None/non-str input produces a validation error rather than a 500.

findings.title: Length guard is unreachable given the allowlist
findings.evidence: ALLOWED_TAGS contains only short ASCII tags, so any tag longer than 40 characters is necessarily absent from the set: the len(tag) > 40 branch can never be the deciding condition and both branches raise the identical message.
findings.evidence_quote: if len(tag) > 40 or tag not in ALLOWED_TAGS:
findings.recommendation: Either drop the length check as redundant (the allowlist already bounds length) or check length first with a distinct message if the intent is to bound input size before membership testing, and add a test that exercises the rejection path.
